summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style entry on Holden, an Australian automobile importer and former manufacturer headquartered in Port Melbourne, Victoria. It traces the company's origins as a South Australian saddlery founded in 1856, its move into automobiles in 1908, and its becoming a General Motors subsidiary in 1931. It also summarizes the company's name changes in 1998 and 2005.
one_line: Holden is an Australian automobile importer and former manufacturer, founded in 1856 as a saddlery and later part of General Motors.
key_facts: Holden is formerly known as General Motors - Holden.
Holden is an Australian automobile importer and former automobile manufacturer.
Holden has its headquarters in Port Melbourne, Victoria.
Holden was founded in 1856 as a saddlery manufacturer in South Australia.
Holden moved into the automotive field in 1908.
Holden became a subsidiary of the United States-based General Motors (GM) in 1931.
In 1931, when Holden became a GM subsidiary, the company was renamed General Motors - Holden's Ltd.
Holden was renamed Holden Ltd in 1998.
Holden was renamed General Motors - Holden in 2005.
